oneTimers: The expected recovery of $986M of IEEPA tariffs (ruled unlawful) is booked inside cost of sales — it lifted gross margin by about 900 basis points and EPS by $0.52, and accounts for most of the jump from last year's $211M net income to this year's $1,069M. It is an expected refund, not cash already received, and it will not repeat.

takeaways.text: The expected recovery of IEEPA tariffs added $986M back into gross profit — roughly 900 basis points of margin and $0.52 of the $0.72 EPS. Strip it out and this was a flat, difficult quarter.
takeaways.title: A tariff refund remade the quarter

takeaways.text: Revenue fell 1% to $11.0B, unevenly: North America grew 3%, but Greater China fell 12% and Converse 32%. Wholesale revenue rose 4% while Nike's own stores and app fell 7%.
takeaways.title: Sales still shrinking

takeaways.text: Gross margin leapt from 40.3% to 49.2% — almost entirely the tariff recovery, an expected refund rather than money already in the bank. It flatters this quarter and will not repeat.
takeaways.title: Margin jumped — on paper

verdict: Nike's sales slipped 1% to $11.0B — but reported profit jumped five-fold to $1.1B, almost entirely because of a $986M expected refund of tariffs that courts ruled unlawful.
